title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Guide, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback Procedures, and Customer Requirements Library
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Comprehensive operational reference for Redwood Private deployments: covers VPC and on‑prem installation patterns, reference architectures, packaging, day‑2 operational procedures, and deterministic upgrade/rollback playbooks. Intended for Solutions, SRE, and Customer Ops teams supporting enterprise customers.
intro: This document consolidates deployment guidance and operational procedures for Redwood Private (VPC and on‑prem) installations. It pairs prescriptive install steps with day‑2 runbooks, upgrade/rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library to streamline sales → delivery → operations handoffs. Use this as the canonical reference while preparing customer engagements and runbooks.
scope_and_audience: Scope: Redwood Private (VPC & on‑prem) deployments, including packaging, networking, security integrations, day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, incident response), and upgrade/rollback. Audience: Solutions Engineers, Customer Ops, SRE, and Security reviewers.
high_level_architecture_overview:
Redwood Private splits into two control planes and runtime components: control-plane (redwood-control) and runtime-plane (redwood-runtime). The control-plane runs optional managed components if customer allows outbound management; the runtime-plane contains inference services, model stores, and caching layers inside customer VPC or on‑prem cluster. Core services: 
- redwood-control: API, auth proxy, telemetry-forwarder (optional) 
- redwood-runtime: model-router, inference-proxy, kv-cache, batching-worker, autoscaler 
- storage: object store (S3-compatible) for models and audit logs 
- networking: internal LB, per-service security groups/ACLs 
- infra components: Postgres for metadata, Redis for transient state, Prometheus/Grafana for observability
reference_architectures:
We publish two validated reference architectures: 
1) VPC Deployment (recommended for cloud-hosted customers): multi-AZ EKS/GKE/AKS cluster, private subnets, NAT for controlled egress, ALB/NLB for internal load balancing, and VPC endpoints for S3/KMS. 
2) On‑Prem (air‑gapped or customer datacenter): bare-metal or virtualized cluster (kubeadm/RKE) with preconfigured NFS/Object gateway, internal PKI, and HSM/KMS integration for key management. 
Each reference includes sizing guidance, network diagrams, and example Terraform modules (see References).
prerequisites_and_customer_requirements_: Before scheduling a deployment, collect the following customer inputs. Use the Customer Requirements Checklist (table below) to validate readiness. Missing items delay delivery and increase risk during upgrades.
customer_requirements_table:
| Area | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Network | Private VPC with at least 3 subnets (control, runtime, management) | Customer must provide subnet IDs, route tables, and peering info |
| Egress policy | NAT or egress gateway with allowed outbound to Redwood control-plane (if enabled) | IP allowlist and FQDNs documented in security addendum |
| DNS | Internal DNS zone or split-horizon DNS for service discovery | Provide domain and records to create |
| Storage | S3-compatible bucket (or NFS/Object Gateway) with 5 TB reserved | Versioning and lifecycle policy recommended |
| Keys | KMS/HSM integration or ability to store keys in local vault | Provide KMS ARN or access instructions |
| Compliance | SOC2/GDPR constraints and approved network audit window | Capture in delivery SOW |

vpc_deployment_quickstart:
Overview: recommended for cloud customers that want a managed Private deployment inside their VPC. This quickstart assumes Terraform and an EKS/GKE/AKS cluster. Steps: 
1) Validate customer prerequisites from the checklist. 
2) Provision infrastructure using redwood-terraform-modules (module: redwood/private-cloud/v1.2). Example: 
   terraform init && terraform apply -var-file=customer-vars.tfvars
3) Deploy control-plane: helm install redwood-control ./charts/control --namespace redwood-system --values control-values.yaml
4) Deploy runtime: helm install redwood-runtime ./charts/runtime --namespace redwood-runtime --values runtime-values.yaml
5) Set up object storage and encryption: configure S3 endpoint and KMS keys in control-values.yaml
6) Run smoke tests: redwoodctl healthcheck --target all; expect status OK for control, runtime, and model-store. 
Rollback tip: If helm install fails, run helm uninstall <release> and inspect Helm hooks/logs. For partial failures, follow the Upgrade and Rollback Procedures section.
onprem_packaging_and_installation:
Redwood on‑prem is distributed as an install bundle (tar.gz) containing: Helm charts, operator image tarballs, and an installer binary (redwood-installer). Packaging supports air‑gapped installs via an offline registry mirror. 
Installation pattern: 
1) Mirror images to local registry: ./mirror-images.sh --bundle redwood-zip --dest registry.internal:5000 
2) Upload artifacts to internal object store (or provide NFS mount) 
3) Run installer: ./redwood-installer install --config customer-config.yaml --kubecontext cluster-local 
4) Validate: redwoodctl status --format json | jq '.services | map(select(.status=="OK"))'
Support notes: Installer includes a preflight check. Common preflight failures: insufficient disk, missing cgroups, or unsupported kernel modules. See Troubleshooting section for fixes.
day2_ops_runbook:
Day‑2 support covers monitoring, backups, scaling, and incident response. Core runbook entries: 
- Monitoring: Ensure Prometheus scraping for /metrics on all services. Default SLOs: 99.9% control-plane uptime, median inference latency < 80ms for small models (measured at 8-token window). Alerts: control-plane_down (P0), high_kv_cache_miss_rate (> 5% sustained 10m, P1), inference_latency_p95 > 500ms (P1). 
- Backups: Postgres daily logical backups (pg_dump) retained 30 days; object-store snapshots daily for model artifacts; store backups in customer-managed long-term storage. 
- Scaling: HorizontalPodAutoscaler on inference-proxy based on request RPS and GPU utilization. Typical HPA config: minReplicas:2 maxReplicas:20 targetGPUUtilizationPercentage:70. 
- Capacity planning: Run monthly capacity reports using rp-capacity-tool to project model churn and peak QPS. 
- Runbook drills: quarterly game-days with simulated pod failure and network partition scenarios. 
Commands: 
- Check health: redwoodctl healthcheck --namespace redwood-runtime 
- Restart service: kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime --namespace redwood-runtime 
- Trigger cache clear: redwoodctl cache flush --scope global
upgrade_and_rollback_procedures:
Principles: deterministic, reversible, and staged. Always perform upgrades in a canary → partial → full pattern with automated health checks. Detailed procedure: 
1) Prepare release: download release tarball and verify checksum. 
2) Canary: deploy new chart release to a canary subset (label: rollout=canary). Monitor key metrics for 30 minutes (error_rate, latency, cache_miss). 
3) Partial rollout: if canary is stable, rollout to 25% of capacity for 1 hour. 
4) Full rollout: progress to 100% using automated Helm/Argo rollouts with health probes. 
Rollback procedure (fast path): 
1) If canary or partial rollout breaches thresholds (error_rate > 0.5% absolute or p95 latency regresses > 2x), immediately trigger an automated abort: argocd app rollback <app> or helm rollback <release> <revision>. 
2) Shift traffic back to previous release using traffic manager (Istio/ALB): set weight previous=100, new=0. 
3) Run post-rollback healthcheck: redwoodctl healthcheck --target all. 
4) Open postmortem and tag the release as failed with rollback_reason in release notes. 
Notes: For DB migrations, use the expand/contract pattern: apply non-blocking schema changes first, then migrate data, then remove legacy columns in a later release. Always test migrations in staging with production-sized datasets.
post_install_validation_and_smoke_tests:
Run the following after any install/upgrade: 
1) redwoodctl healthcheck --target control-plane (expect OK on 3/3 readiness probes) 
2) Run sample inference: curl -X POST https://<ingress>/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}' and assert 200 and non-empty text. 
3) Run a model load test: rp-loadtest --model small-llm --concurrency 50 --duration 60s and ensure p95 < 200ms for small models. 
4) Verify metrics: Prometheus query 'up{job~="redwood.*"}' returns all services up.
common_troubleshooting:
Preflight failures: 
- Disk space: increase /var/lib or mount additional volume; ensure ext4/xfs supported. 
- Kernel modules: enable ipvs or overlayfs if pod networking fails. 
- Image pull errors (air‑gapped): verify mirror registry credentials and image tags in helm values. 
Runtime issues: 
- High KV cache miss rate: increase cache RAM or tune LRU policy (values: 'cache.enabled=true' and 'cache.size=24GB'). 
- Postgres slow queries: add read replicas and index the metadata tables (queries: model_versions, rollout_status).
